overview: HCLTech is a Noida, India-headquartered global IT services and engineering company, among the largest in India by market capitalization, operating through three reporting segments: IT and Business Services (ITBS), Engineering and R&D Services (ERS), and HCLSoftware (enterprise products and platforms). The company serves Global 2000 enterprises across financial services, manufacturing, life sciences and healthcare, technology, telecom, retail, and public services, with roughly 227,000 employees across 60 countries. Fiscal year ends March 31; FY2026 (ended March 31, 2026) revenue was ₹130,144 crore (~$15.7B), with the US, Europe and India as its core geographic markets.

business_model.summary: HCLTech earns the large majority of revenue from long-duration, contract-based IT services (application development/management, cloud, cybersecurity, BPO) billed on time-and-materials or fixed-price/outcome-based models, supplemented by an engineering services (ERS) business serving OEMs on product/chip design, and a smaller but higher-margin recurring-revenue software (HCLSoftware) business with ~$1.0B of Annual Recurring Revenue. Pricing is increasingly shifting toward outcome-based and platform/IP-led consumption models as AI reshapes traditional labor-based delivery.
business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise — primarily Global 2000 and large/mid-market enterprises; 23 clients each contribute $100M+ annually (FY26) and 976 clients contribute $1M+, indicating a long tail with meaningful concentration at the top
business_model.geographic_mix: Services revenue growth by geography (FY26, constant currency YoY): USA +2.3%, Europe +4.5%, India +5.7%, Rest of World +17.8%. Core markets are US, UK and Nordics; Focus markets include Japan, Canada, Germany; New Frontier/high-growth markets include India, Mexico, South Korea

competitive_position.market_position: Third-largest India-based IT services company by revenue (behind TCS and Infosys), but has delivered the fastest constant-currency revenue growth among large-cap comparable peers for three consecutive years (FY24-FY26), outpacing TCS and Infosys on topline growth while trailing TCS on scale and profitability ratios

moat_factors.description: Multi-decade engineering pedigree (chip-to-cloud) gives HCLTech leadership recognition in 52 of 54 industry ER&D benchmarks, a differentiator versus more BPO/applications-weighted peers
HCLSoftware (~$1B ARR) and ERS provide diversification away from pure-play commoditized IT services, though software revenue has recently declined
Multi-year outsourcing contracts and deep embedding in client core systems (SAP, mainframe modernization) create moderate switching costs, though not as strong as network effects
227,000+ employees across 60 countries and an asset-light offshore-heavy delivery model support cost competitiveness versus Accenture/IBM but is matched by TCS/Infosys/Cognizant

First India-headquartered large-cap to disclose Advanced AI revenue ($620M annualized FY26, $876M by Q2 FY27); partnerships with OpenAI, NVIDIA, Microsoft, AWS; unclear if this is durable differentiation or catch-up with global peers

weaknesses: Smaller scale than TCS and Accenture limits pricing leverage on mega-deals
HCLSoftware revenue has been declining (-4.1% YoY in FY26), undermining the recurring-revenue diversification thesis
Heavy dependence on discretionary technology spending by Western enterprises, which has been soft/cautious through FY25-FY26
AI-led pricing deflation in traditional services (ADM, BPO) requires replacement revenue streams to sustain growth
High client/geography concentration risk despite diversification efforts (USA still the largest single market)

growth_drivers: Advanced AI revenue scaling rapidly — $620M annualized in FY26, $876M by Q2 FY27 — spanning AI Factory, Physical AI, Agentic AI, AI Engineering and Custom Silicon
AI Force 2.0 platform deployed across 75+ priority client accounts, converting into large strategic contract wins
Record new deal bookings: $9.3B total contract value in FY26, $3.3B in Q2 FY27 alone
Engineering-led growth vectors in semiconductors and Physical AI/robotics, capturing rising R&D outsourcing demand

Acquisitions to deepen software/data capabilities: Zeenea, Wobby (AI data analyst), pending Jaspersoft ($240M, embedded analytics), and HPE Telco Solutions Business ($160M) plus prior HPE Communications Technology Group integration
Expansion into mid-market enterprises (a $400B+ segment) and Global Capability Center (GCC) set-up/transformation services for clients like Western Union and Commonwealth Bank of Australia
Sovereign AI/cloud demand from governments and regulated industries (banking, healthcare, public sector)
Geographic expansion into high-velocity markets (India, Mexico, South Korea) alongside steady core markets (US, UK, Nordics) and focus markets (Japan, Canada, Germany)

business.risk: AI/GenAI disruption to core services model
business.description: Company explicitly flags that AI-native delivery models and automation could replace tasks currently performed by humans, reducing demand for traditional services, compressing utilization and pricing power, and enabling client insourcing

Despite diversification into software and ERS, concentration in certain segments, industries and geographies remains a disclosed strategic risk; top accounts ($100M+ clients: 23 in FY26) represent an outsized share of revenue
HCLSoftware revenue fell 4.1% YoY in constant currency in FY26, raising questions about competitiveness of the products business against larger enterprise software vendors
IT services voluntary attrition at 12.5% (among lowest in industry) but shortage of AI-skilled talent and rising costs to hire/retain AI SMEs could pressure margins and delivery quality
Competes against larger-scale TCS and Accenture as well as Infosys, Cognizant and Wipro, all pursuing similar AI-led transformation strategies, risking commoditization of GenAI offerings

financial.description: Revenue is predominantly USD/GBP/EUR-denominated while costs are significantly INR-denominated; reported rupee results and reported dividends are affected by INR/USD and cross-currency moves, and constant-currency growth has recently diverged meaningfully from reported growth

FY26 included a ₹956 crore one-time impact from India's New Labour Codes, and Q4 FY26 standalone results included a ₹5,733 crore one-time Bilateral Advance Pricing Agreement (BAPA) tax-related impact, both reducing reported net income versus underlying performance

financial.risk: High capital return reduces reinvestment flexibility
financial.description: The company returned 97.6% of net income as dividends in FY26 (above its 75% minimum commitment), which, combined with ongoing M&A, could pressure the balance sheet if organic growth disappoints

regulatory.description: A proposed/enacted $100,000 H-1B visa fee under the Trump administration could raise costs for US onsite staffing; analyst estimates suggest a modest 10-50bps margin impact industry-wide with partial client pass-through, but could accelerate further offshoring to India-based delivery (a net positive for utilization but risk to onsite-fee revenue)

EU AI Act, data sovereignty/localization rules and emerging AI liability frameworks increase compliance costs and could constrain how HCLTech deploys GenAI/agentic solutions for regulated clients (banking, healthcare, government)

regulatory.risk: India labour code and tax regime changes
regulatory.description: FY26 New Labour Codes already caused a one-time ₹956 crore hit; further Indian regulatory changes (labor, transfer pricing/APA) could create similar episodic impacts

macro.description: Management explicitly cites 'continued softness in discretionary technology spending by global enterprises' as a FY26 headwind; revenue growth of 3.9-4.8% constant currency came in below long-run averages amid macro caution
Management repeatedly cites 'geopolitical volatility' as a factor shaping demand uncertainty and risk posture across FY26 and into FY27
As a B2B enterprise services provider, HCLTech's revenue is correlated with global (especially US/European) corporate IT budgets, which are cut first in a recession
Indirect sensitivity via client capex/IT budget decisions and INR currency translation of USD-denominated contracts

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global technology/IT services market is viewed by management as a multi-trillion-dollar, structurally growing market, but near-term (FY26-FY27) demand is described as 'steady' rather than robust, with enterprise spending balancing cost discipline against AI-led transformation investment. Global enterprise infrastructure services market projected to exceed $450B by 2030; engineering services addressable market projected to reach $650B by 2030.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — IT services spending is discretionary and tracks corporate earnings/capex cycles; the FY25-FY26 period reflected a cautious, below-trend demand environment despite resilient long-term secular growth from digital/AI transformation
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect — higher rates can dampen client capex/discretionary tech budgets, especially for BFSI clients (a top vertical at 21.4% of FY26 vertical mix)

recent_developments.event: Reported revenue of ₹35,620 crore (+11.5% YoY, +2.6% YoY constant currency), net profit up 21.2% YoY to ₹5,132 crore, EBIT margin improved to 18.2%; record net new deal bookings of $3.3 billion; annualized Advanced AI revenue reached $876 million; raised lower end of FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 2.5-4.0% (from 1.0-4.0%), maintained EBIT margin guidance at 17.5-18.5%; stock rallied ~4.7% on the results

FY26 revenue ₹130,144 crore (+11.2% YoY), net income ₹16,652 crore (reported, including one-time New Labour Codes impact); ex-exceptional EBIT ₹22,397 crore (17.2% margin); services revenue +12.1% YoY; HCLSoftware revenue +2.9% YoY (reported) but -4.1% YoY in constant currency; declared total FY26 dividend of ₹60/share (97.6% of net income); Q4 FY26 standalone results hit by a one-time ₹5,733 crore Bilateral Advance Pricing Agreement (BAPA) tax impact

M&A push: agreed to acquire HPE's Telco Solutions Business (~$160M, building on 2024 HPE Communications Technology Group integration) and entered agreement to acquire Jaspersoft (~$240M, embedded analytics, pending regulatory approval); also acquired Wobby (AI data analyst bots, Antwerp) and Zeenea, and Singapore-based Finergic (core banking/wealth management)

First Indian IT firm to report over $100 million quarterly Advanced AI revenue; record deal bookings of $2.6-3.3 billion range across quarters; continued momentum in GenAI/Agentic AI deal conversion via AI Force platform

US H-1B visa fee proposals (up to ~$100,000-103,000 per petition) created an industry-wide overhang for Indian IT services firms including HCLTech, though estimated margin impact (10-50bps) is modest and partially offset by accelerated offshoring/GCC buildout

50th anniversary of HCL Group; company reiterated ambition to be 'the world's best AI solutions provider,' with AI Force deployed across 75+ client accounts and over 144,000 employees trained in GenAI (11,800+ certified AI Builders, 700+ Blackbelt-certified)

items.notes: Raised from prior 1.0%-4.0% range; lower end lifted by 150bps following strong Q2 FY27 bookings; includes ~87bps inorganic contribution from recent acquisitions
Includes ~62bps inorganic contribution; organic growth outlook broadly unchanged at the midpoint
Unchanged from prior guidance despite the revenue guidance raise, reflecting continued investment in AI capabilities and sales/marketing (Project Ascend cost program funding reinvestment)

Actual payout ratios were 93.4% (FY25) and 97.6%/87.8% (FY26, reported/ex-exceptional); company has a 10-decade (actually multi-year) track record of top-quartile TSR and consistent quarterly dividends (91+ consecutive quarters)

items.target: no specific numeric target disclosed; trajectory highlighted
items.notes: Grew from $620M annualized (FY26 year-end) to $876M annualized by Q2 FY27; management treats this as a key proof point of AI-led growth strategy rather than a formal guided KPI

guidance.management_commentary: CEO C Vijayakumar and Chairperson Roshni Nadar Malhotra both describe FY26 as delivered 'against a backdrop of cautious technology services spending, macro-economic uncertainty and geopolitical volatility,' with the company outperforming comparable peers on constant-currency growth for a third consecutive year. Management remains confident in executing its AI growth strategy and creating long-term shareholder value, while explicitly flagging headwinds from technology transformation (AI-led deflation of traditional services) and geopolitical uncertainty. The FY27 guidance raise after Q2 results signals improving confidence in the demand environment moving into H2 FY27.

bull_case: Fastest constant-currency revenue growth among large-cap India IT peers for three consecutive years (FY24-FY26), demonstrating differentiated execution versus TCS, Infosys and Wipro
Diversified three-segment model (ITBS, ERS, HCLSoftware) provides some insulation versus pure-play IT services peers, with ERS exposed to secular semiconductor/Physical AI demand

Early, credible AI positioning — first India-headquartered large-cap to report Advanced AI revenue, which nearly 1.4x'd from $620M to $876M annualized within two quarters, plus marquee partnerships (OpenAI, NVIDIA, Microsoft, AWS)

Disciplined capital returns (near-full payout of net income, 91+ consecutive quarterly dividends) and high ROIC (40.3% in FY26, up from 28.9% in FY22) support a shareholder-friendly, high free-cash-flow profile (FCF-to-net-income conversion of 119% over 5 years)
Raised FY27 revenue guidance after Q2 results signals improving order book momentum ($9.3B TCV in FY26, $3.3B in a single Q2 FY27 quarter) despite a still-cautious macro backdrop
bear_case: AI-led pricing deflation is a structural, company-acknowledged threat to the core labor-arbitrage IT services model, and it is not yet clear new AI-native revenue streams will fully offset erosion in legacy ADM/BPO/testing services
HCLSoftware, the highest-margin and most diversifying segment, saw revenue decline 4.1% YoY in constant currency in FY26 — a warning sign that the products business is losing ground competitively

Discretionary enterprise technology spending has been soft since FY25, and a global recession or prolonged spending caution in the US/Europe (the core markets) would disproportionately hit growth given revenue concentration
US H-1B visa fee increases and broader immigration policy uncertainty create a persistent regulatory overhang for an industry still reliant on onsite US staffing and visa-dependent delivery models

Valuation and analyst sentiment are mixed-to-cautious: 2026 price targets and ratings have diverged widely across brokerages (from Sell at Citi/JPMorgan to Buy at Jefferies/Nomura), reflecting genuine uncertainty about whether HCLTech's AI narrative will translate into durable premium growth versus being priced for perfection
